thread.title: Victor Eklund earns first NHL point in debut game for Islanders
thread.title_full: Victor Eklund earns first NHL point in debut game for Islanders

author: c. n. coughlin
title: Victor Eklund earns first NHL point in debut game for Islanders
text:
Victor Eklund recorded his first National Hockey League point during his debut game for the New York Islanders on April 15. The 18-year-old, who was selected 16th overall in the 2025 NHL Draft, assisted on Bo Horvat’s goal to tie the score against the Carolina Hurricanes in the second period. Despite Eklund’s contribution, the Islanders lost their season finale 2-1.
Eklund described his debut as a memorable experience. “It was the craziest game of my life,” Eklund said. “Having been young, playing the video games and just now [to] be out there playing with with Horvat and and all the other guys, it’s crazy.”
The assist came on Horvat’s milestone 300th career goal. However, Horvat insisted that Eklund should keep the puck from this significant moment. “He’s going to have to fight me over it because I am not taking that puck,” Horvat said. “It’s not only special to play in the NHL, but to get a point. You’ll never forget your first one.”
Eklund played alongside Horvat and Simon Holmstrom and also appeared on the team’s top power-play unit during his first outing. Head Coach Pete DeBoer commented positively about Eklund’s performance: “[Eklund is a] really skilled kid,” DeBoer said. “He’s got a great motor. He reminds me a little bit of Logan Stankoven, who I had in Dallas for a year. He’s got a bright future.”
Eklund finished with one assist, two shots on goal, two hits, and logged over fifteen minutes of ice time in his debut match.
Reflecting on his experience after the game, Eklund said: “I had the best time of my life… so much fun. Obviously a really good league, and I think it went pretty well.”
